sources.title: Ministry of Economy and Labour, Department of Immigration, Work Permit Policy 2025 (5 June 2025; copy held by Bernews, the gov.bm copy returning 404)
sources.said: 7.7 Musician orEntertainer Work permits for foreign musicians/entertainers to perform at commercial locations open to the public (clubs, pubs and hotels) may be granted, provided they are advertised in the normal way. The maximum period for a work permit in the entertainment industry will normally be a Seasonal Work Permit of eight (8) months. However, where a one-off large, commercial entertainment event open to the public is to be held and foreign musicians/entertainers are to be utilised, qualified Bermudian(s), Spouse(s) of Bermudians and PRC holder(s) musician(s)/entertainer(s) of the same entertainment genre must feature in the entertainment event. … Promoters and event organizers must also contact the Bermuda Entertainment Union (bermudaentertainmentunion.com) to provide notification of the event, obtain approval and pay any required dues. … Standard, Seasonal and Occasional Work Permits Thirty (30) working days

sources.title: Government of Bermuda, All Immigration Fees
sources.said: One-year standard or periodic work permit $1,015.00 … Short-term permit for a person to be engaged for a single period of 14 days or less, in professional sport or entertainment: (a) per person (up to 5 persons) $400.00 (b) per group of more than 5 persons in addition to the fee at (A) above, for each person beyond the fifth $200.00

blockers.sought: whether a Seasonal Work Permit for an entertainer can be renewed

tried.institution: Work Permit Policy 2025 section 7.7 says the maximum is 'normally' eight months and says nothing of renewal; gov.bm's own PDF of the policy and of the Entertainment Policy return 404 for this client

note: The Work Permit Policy of 5 June 2025 (section 7.7) grants foreign musicians and entertainers work permits, normally at most a Seasonal Work Permit of eight months, advertised in the normal way; a one-off large public event must feature qualified Bermudians of the same genre and its promoter must notify the Bermuda Entertainment Union, obtain approval and pay dues. A single engagement of 14 days or less in professional entertainment has its own short-term permit fee ($400 a person). The fee schedule names no Seasonal Work Permit fee apart, so the one-year standard permit's fee is given beside the 14-day one. Bermuda's dollar is at par with the US dollar.
